html:
The Seminole Nation of Oklahoma is the government of the Seminole people removed from Florida to Oklahoma, with its capital at Wewoka. The map draws its small territory in 1492, but the Seminole only arrived here in the 1830s and 1840s.

The Seminole formed in Florida in the 1700s from Creek migrants and the remnants of older peoples. They took in many Black people who had escaped slavery, the Black Seminoles. In the Seminole Wars the United States fought for decades to move them west. Most were shipped to Indian Territory and placed at first among the Muscogee (Creek), a removal that was part of the Trail of Tears. A few hundred stayed in the Everglades; their descendants form the Seminole Tribe of Florida.

The Seminole Nation got its own land in 1856 and later lost most of it to allotment. Its freedmen, descendants of Black Seminoles, are still part of the nation, though their rights have been disputed.
